chunks: Ali ibn Isma'il al-Mithamini from al-Hasan ibn Ali from some of his companions from al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

The elder brother is in the position of the father. The implication in this report is that he is in the position of the father regarding the obligation of honoring him, submitting to his commands, and returning to his obedience. It is not meant that he is in the position of the father regarding the permissibility of contracting him to his younger sister without her consent, nor regarding seeking her opinion, based on what we have previously presented. And if it were explicit in that, we would interpret it as being due to taqiyya (dissimulation), because that is the view of some of the Sunnis.

key_terms.بِمَنزِلَةِ الأَبِ: in the position of the father

ai.seo_question: Does an elder brother have the right to marry off his younger sister without her consent according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi uses this narration from Imam al-Rida to distinguish between the general honor and obedience due to an elder brother (makanat al-ab) and the specific legal authority (wilayah) required for marriage contracting. He notes that if the text were interpreted as granting full paternal authority, it would likely be understood as *taqiyya* (dissimulation) to align with the view of some Sunni jurists who held that a brother could marry off his sister without her consent.
